Absolute risk with a model that changes at a cut age

Source: R/compute_absolute_risk_split_interval.R
computeAbsoluteRiskSplitInterval.Rd

Estimates absolute risks over an age interval when the relative-risk model, the covariate profiles or the reference population change at a cut age (for example, different log relative risks before and after menopause). The interval \([a, a + \tau)\) is split at the cut age \(c\); the first model gives the risk \(AR_1\) over \([a, c)\) and the probability \(S_1\) of reaching age \(c\) alive and free of the disease, the second model gives the risk \(AR_2\) over \([c, a + \tau)\), and the risk over the whole interval is $$AR = AR_1 + S_1 AR_2.$$ With the same model on both sides and a whole-number cut age, this equals the risk from computeAbsoluteRisk() over the whole interval for profiles without missing risk factors. (A fractional cut age splits a year of age, within which the yearly risk model is not exactly additive, so the two can then differ very slightly.) (Earlier versions combined the parts as \(AR_1 + (1 - AR_1) AR_2\), which ignores deaths from competing causes before the cut age and overstates the risk.)

Usage

computeAbsoluteRiskSplitInterval(
  apply.age.start,
  apply.age.interval.length,
  apply.cov.profile,
  model.formula,
  model.disease.incidence.rates,
  model.log.RR,
  model.ref.dataset,
  model.ref.dataset.weights = NULL,
  model.cov.info,
  model.competing.incidence.rates = NULL,
  return.lp = FALSE,
  apply.snp.profile = NULL,
  model.snp.info = NULL,
  model.bin.fh.name = NULL,
  cut.time = NULL,
  apply.cov.profile.2 = NULL,
  model.formula.2 = NULL,
  model.log.RR.2 = NULL,
  model.ref.dataset.2 = NULL,
  model.ref.dataset.weights.2 = NULL,
  model.cov.info.2 = NULL,
  model.bin.fh.name.2 = NULL,
  n.imp = 5,
  return.refs.risk = FALSE,
  ...
)

Arguments

apply.age.start

Age(s) at the start of the risk interval: a single value or one per profile. Fractional ages are allowed.

apply.age.interval.length

Length(s) of the risk interval in years: a single value or one per profile. Fractional lengths are allowed.

apply.cov.profile

A data frame of covariate profiles (columns matched by name; extra columns are ignored); missing values are allowed.

model.formula

A formula such as Y ~ x1 + as.factor(x2) + x1:x3 describing the design matrix of the relative-risk model. The response is ignored. Leave NULL (with the other covariate arguments) for a SNP-only model.

model.disease.incidence.rates

Age-specific annual incidence rates: a two-column table (integer age, rate) or a three-column table (start age, end age, annual rate in that age band). Must cover consecutive ages including every year of age used by the risk intervals.

model.log.RR

Log relative risks of the design-matrix columns (no intercept), as a named vector or a one-column matrix with row names; the names must be the column names that model.formula generates.

model.ref.dataset

A data frame of risk factors for a sample representing the population, with no missing values. Columns are matched to the covariates by name.

model.ref.dataset.weights

Optional non-negative sampling weights of the rows of model.ref.dataset (normalized internally).

model.cov.info

A list with one element per covariate of model.formula, each a list with fields name (the covariate name), type ("continuous" or "factor") and, for factors, levels (all levels) and optionally ref (the referent level).

model.competing.incidence.rates

Age-specific annual rates of competing mortality, in the same layouts. NULL means no competing mortality.

return.lp

If TRUE, also return the linear predictors.

apply.snp.profile

A matrix or data frame of genotypes (risk-allele counts 0, 1, 2 or NA), one column per SNP of model.snp.info, matched by name when the columns are named after all the SNPs and by position when they are named after none (naming only some is an error). If NULL, all SNPs are treated as missing.

model.snp.info

A data frame with columns snp.name, snp.odds.ratio (per-allele odds ratio) and snp.freq (risk-allele frequency).

model.bin.fh.name

Name of the binary family-history covariate (see computeAbsoluteRisk()); NULL or NA when not applicable.

cut.time

Cut age(s) at which the model changes: a single value or one per profile.

apply.cov.profile.2, model.formula.2, model.log.RR.2, model.ref.dataset.2, model.ref.dataset.weights.2, model.cov.info.2, model.bin.fh.name.2

The model after the cut age (see Details).

n.imp

Number of simulated SNP genotype sets of the reference population (1 to 20).

return.refs.risk

If TRUE, also return the risks of each model's reference population over the first profile's part of the interval.

...

Not used. The removed argument use.c.code is accepted with a deprecation warning and ignored.

Value

An object of class "icareSplit", a list with

  • risk: one-column matrix (Risk_Estimate) of absolute risks;

  • details: data frame with the start of the interval (Int_Start), the age at which the second model starts (Cut_Age), the end of the interval (Int_End), the covariate profile and the risk;

  • lps.1, lps.2: linear predictors of both models (if return.lp);

  • refs.risk.1, refs.risk.2: reference risks of both models (if return.refs.risk).

Without a cut age and second model, the result of computeAbsoluteRisk() with class "icareSplit".

Details

Arguments ending in .2 describe the model after the cut age; each one left NULL is taken from its counterpart before the cut age (the reference weights are reused with the reference dataset). The disease and competing incidence rates, the SNP information and n.imp are shared. If cut.time is outside a profile's interval, that profile's risk comes from one model only. If no .2 argument and no cut.time is given, this is computeAbsoluteRisk() over the whole interval.

For profiles with missing risk factors, \(AR_1\), \(S_1\) and \(AR_2\) are each averaged over the reference population of their model (the two models may have different reference datasets, so the missing values cannot be completed jointly). The result can therefore differ slightly from the risk over the whole interval even when both models are the same; in the bundled example the relative difference is below 0.1%.

See also

computeAbsoluteRisk()

Examples

data(bc_data, package = "iCARE")

# Risk from age 40 to 80 with different log relative risks after age 50
results <- computeAbsoluteRiskSplitInterval(
  model.formula = bc_model_formula,
  model.cov.info = bc_model_cov_info,
  model.log.RR = bc_model_log_or,
  model.log.RR.2 = bc_model_log_or_post_50,
  model.ref.dataset = ref_cov_dat,
  model.ref.dataset.2 = ref_cov_dat_post_50,
  model.disease.incidence.rates = bc_inc,
  model.competing.incidence.rates = mort_inc,
  apply.age.start = 40,
  apply.age.interval.length = 40,
  cut.time = 50,
  apply.cov.profile = new_cov_prof
)
results
#> Absolute risks of 3 profiles
#> 
#>   Int_Start Cut_Age Int_End Risk_Estimate
#> 1        40      50      80    0.12393471
#> 2        40      50      80    0.08796538
#> 3        40      50      80    0.13718498
#> Profiles and risks: `$details`; risks: `$risk`.
